who: Panipak Wongpattanakit and coach Choi Young-seok · Thailand
quote: Korean coach Choi Young-seok has led Thailand's taekwondo team since 2002. In 2021 his athlete Panipak Wongpattanakit won Thailand's first Olympic taekwondo gold.
meaning: Patient work with the right coach can lift a whole team.

who: Ananda to the Buddha · Shurangama Sutra, tr. Charles Luk, 1966
quote: ...although I have listened to His profound words, I am still unawakened as if I had not heard them.
meaning: You can hear great teaching many times and still not get it.

who: Wang Yangming · Instructions for Practical Living 5, tr. Wing-tsit Chan, 1963
quote: There have never been people who know but do not act. Those who are supposed to know but do not act simply do not yet know.
meaning: If you know it but cannot do it, you don't really know it yet.

who: The wheelwright Pian · Zhuangzi, Book XIII, tr. James Legge, 1891
quote: ...there is a knack in it. I cannot teach the knack to my son, nor can my son learn it from me.
meaning: Some skills cannot be passed on by talking. You must feel them yourself.

who: The Buddha · Shurangama Sutra, tr. Charles Luk, 1966
quote: ...a man pointing a finger at the moon to show it to others... If they look at the finger and mistake it for the moon, they lose (sight of) both the moon and the finger.
meaning: The teacher's words point the way. Don't stare at the words; look.

who: Aristotle · Nicomachean Ethics II.4, tr. W. D. Ross
quote: ...most people... take refuge in theory... behaving somewhat like patients who listen attentively to their doctors, but do none of the things they are ordered to do.
meaning: Listening to good advice does nothing if you never do it.

who: Zhuangzi · Book XVII, tr. James Legge, 1891
quote: An insect of the summer cannot be talked with about ice... it knows nothing beyond its own season.
meaning: Some things you can't understand until your time comes.

who: The Buddha · Dhammapada 19, tr. F. Max Müller
quote: The thoughtless man, even if he can recite a large portion (of the law), but is not a doer of it... is like a cowherd counting the cows of others.
meaning: Knowing the words by heart is not owning them. Doing them is.

who: Laozi · Tao Te Ching 56, tr. James Legge, 1891
quote: He who knows (the Tao) does not (care to) speak (about it); he who is (ever ready to) speak about it does not know it.
meaning: People who really know talk less. Big talkers often don't know.

quote: For sheep don't throw up the grass to show the shepherds how much they have eaten; but, inwardly digesting their food, they outwardly produce wool and milk.
meaning: Don't show off what you learned. Let it show in what you do.
